Hakon.narrative: I was born among Brandholm's timber and learned to set a beam straight from my father, Halvard. I chose Rose and a home here at Oathstone, where the berry bushes need tending and both towns have something to say about us. I want the planted ground left in peace; a hunt that feeds one town should not trample another's winter food.
goals: Protect the berry fields from hunters crossing them
Keep trade between the towns steady enough for Oathstone to live through winter
Give my children room to belong to both sides
Hakon.mood: Wary and stubborn, with pride in the household he has made.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees what each town costs us, and still makes this home feel whole.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: son
relations.note: He hears the taunts more than he lets on; I wish I could mend that with my hands.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She can make a game of any patch of earth.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: daughter

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: father

relations.name: Astrid

relations.name: Tamsin

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He follows Brann's hunt across our bushes and calls it necessity.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: His hunters cross the planted ground as if the Oath were only words.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She has kept the stone neutral longer than most of us have kept our tempers.

memories.gist: When I first came back to Oathstone with Rose, the gossip followed us to the berry ring. We planted anyway, one bush at a time.
Halvard showed me how to brace a roof beam so it would hold through a winter wind. I still use his way of checking the join.
I found fresh tracks and broken berry stems where Kjell's hunters had crossed the fields. I was angry enough to go looking for him, but the bushes needed tending first.
At a trade day, I heard Brandholm and Saltreach speak of the same Oath as if it belonged to different people. I went home to Rose wondering what our children would be taught.

stances.why: Our household lives between the towns; breaking the agreement would make that a danger, not a home.
Berries are stored food, and trampled bushes do not grow back in time for winter.
Wynn, Asa and Linnet should not have to choose a side to be accepted by their kin.

Rose.narrative: I learned to keep a fire and dress a wound in Saltreach, and I still carry those habits into the fields and the sickroom here. Hakon and I have made a life at Oathstone, though Ilse has never forgiven me for marrying a Brandholm man. I want the children fed, the bushes growing, and people treated before old quarrels decide they are enemies.
goals: Keep the household healthy and supplied through the seasons
Help the berry fields recover where hunters have trampled them
Make room for my children to know their kin in both towns
Rose.mood: Patient but tired of being judged for a marriage that is her own.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He works hard for this place, even when the towns make him feel he must defend it.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is old enough to notice every slight and young enough to think each one is his fault.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows me among the plants and asks what every leaf is for.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her little hands grab at anything within reach.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He knows why I chose Hakon, though he misses having me nearer.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She sees my marriage as a betrayal, and I cannot make her grief smaller by arguing.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She does not ask me to account for which town I came from before she helps.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She gives each side a hearing, and that matters here.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: niece
relations.note: She brings me shells and stones as if each were a small patient.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She misses her son and makes a fuss over the children when she visits.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: father-in-law
relations.note: He has made room for me in his family, though I know the old wound between our towns still weighs on him.

memories.gist: When I left Saltreach to marry Hakon, I knew people would talk. Ilse's coldness still stung when we met afterward.
Fen and I once worked through a long night caring for a feverish child; by dawn we were both too tired to speak plainly.
A hunter's tracks cut through the berry rows, and Hakon came back angry. I checked the damaged plants and counted which might still bear fruit.
The children sat together with Kit and traded little stones and shells. For a while nobody asked which town any of them belonged to.

stances.why: A wound does not wait for people to settle who started the quarrel.
Both towns need what the other has, and Oathstone is where they can still meet safely.
Their parents' birthplaces are not a fault the children should inherit.

Wynn.narrative: I live by the stone with my mother, father, Asa and Linnet. Some children say I am from the wrong town, whichever town they are standing in. I like when Kit comes to visit, because then we can look for shells and stones instead of listening to grown people argue.
goals: Play with Kit when she visits
Help with the berry bushes without breaking them
Find a place where children from either town will play with me
Wynn.mood: Curious, a little stung by teasing, and glad of familiar company.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: father
relations.note: He gets cross about the bushes, but he lets me help him mend things.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She knows what to do when someone is hurt.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She follows me around until I make up a game.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: sister
relations.note: I can make her laugh by pulling faces.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She brings the best shells, and we both like odd stones.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: grandfather
relations.note: He knows how to make wood fit together.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She’s kind when I visit, and she tells me what Brandholm was like before I was born.

memories.gist: Some children teased me about being from both towns. I kept thinking about it after they had gone to play somewhere else.
Kit and I looked for shells and smooth stones together and sorted them by shape.
Father showed me a damaged berry bush and told me which part might grow again if we left it alone.

stances.why: My family came from each town, so it feels wrong when someone says I can only belong to one.
The grown-ups need the berries, and a broken bush cannot be fixed like a toy.

Asa.narrative: I live with Mama and Papa by the big grey stone. Wynn shows me the berry bushes, and I like to stay near Linnet. Sometimes people talk loudly, but Mama has warm food and Papa is home.
Asa.mood: Content and watchful when voices rise.

Linnet.narrative: Warm arms. A voice I know. Light moves on the grey stone, and someone lifts me when I fuss.
goals: Be held when I am upset
